name: Integrity, audit and safety
summary: Who wrote what and how to undo it, write permissions, staged review, attestations, secrets, snapshots and answer checks.

features.name: Write ledger and undo
features.summary: Records each note write by agent and device with a before-image, and plans a sealed undo per agent or path.
capabilities: Logs one `note-write` event per create, update, append or revert: agent, device, target, sha256 of both sides
Keeps replaced bytes as `write-images/<sha256>` in vault or device-local state, so a write can be undone
Lists writes newest first, filtered by agent, device, path, operation and time window (`brain writes`)
Folds note-write and write-session events into one row per destination with agents and devices (last 7 days)
Plans a revert by agent, device or path sealed by a digest; `--apply <digest>` re-plans and snapshots first
Returns a read-only sealed revert plan over MCP (`brain_writes` `plan_revert`); only the CLI applies it
Refuses a target on drift, an interleaved unselected write, a missing before-image or unreadable bytes
Reports the first broken line per legacy Brain log shard by its `prev`/`h` hash chain (`brain log verify`)
Prunes before-images older than 30 days by default (`writes prune-images --older-than-days`, with `--dry-run`)
limits: Log events on a machine switched to the store carry no hash chain; `log verify` walks legacy day files only
Signal slugs and daily logs emit no write event, so the destination list can miss writes and says so
An event names the writing process's configured agent, for a token caller's write too; it is unauthenticated
No three-way merge: a target another writer touched is refused, not merged

features.name: Write permissions and freeze
features.summary: A permissions document, an owner-write gate, a global write freeze and host deny rules that keep agents off brain files.
capabilities: Resolves guarded writes against the permissions document (`_permissions.yaml` or `permissions.document`)
Ranks matching entries, then agent override, role, default_action; deny beats ask beats allow at equal scope
Dry-runs the decision table per declared agent (`permissions show`)
Queries recorded gate decisions by actor, action, verdict, time window and limit (`permissions ledger`)
Stops every content writer with a `frozen.json` marker (`brain freeze`, CLI only), even an unreadable one
Writes deny rules for Brain preferences, retired, log, snapshots and `_brain.yaml` into Claude Code or Codex
Removes manifest-recorded deny and allow entries, or Codex's current rules if none (`brain unprotect`)
Backs up `.claude/settings.json` or `settings.local.json` before a file tool writes it; denies if that fails
Refuses or warns on a caller-named foreign `owner:` per `integrity.owner_scope_writes` (default off)
limits: On a machine switched to the store the freeze marker is device-local and freezes that machine only
Native deny rules exist only for Claude Code and Codex
The host-settings backup hook is off by default and denies nothing when bun or the hook script is missing
With no permissions document every gate behaves as before; an unreadable document refuses instead

features.name: Staged review of agent writes
features.summary: Optionally stages agent note creates and ingest pages for operator approval before they are published.
capabilities: Stages captured signals in `Brain/pending/` instead of the inbox while `write_approval.enabled` is on
Stages note creates (`write_approval.notes`) and ingest summaries (`write_approval.ingest`) in their own lanes
Without a permissions document, reads the lane key (notes, ingest), then the master key; env beats config
Lists every lane sorted and names unreadable entries with a reason (`pending list --lane`)
Publishes an entry unchanged to its target by exclusive create (`pending apply`); `--dry-run` writes nothing
Moves a rejected entry into `Brain/retired/` with the given reason (`pending reject --reason`)
Keeps staged documents out of the search index, so recall cannot surface an unreviewed write
Once switched, records signals as `signal-state` and note or ingest entries as `lane-entry` store records
limits: Off by default; once a permissions document exists, its `ask` and `deny` decide and the keys are ignored
Review is CLI-only; no MCP tool lists, applies or rejects a staged entry
Only note creates are staged in the notes lane; updates and appends publish directly

features.name: Signed store attestations
features.summary: Ed25519-signed attestations of the legacy Brain log heads and ledgers, verified shard by shard.
capabilities: Creates an operator Ed25519 keypair in `.open-second-brain/keys/attestation/`, optionally passphrase-wrapped
Measures the vault id, one chain head per Brain log shard, ledger file names and the index's embedding stamp
Embeds the manifest sha256 in a sealed record per run, then Ed25519-signs the whole record; never mints a key
Verifies against the newest attestation per shard: intact, appended (valid forward chain), diverged or missing
Checks the signature with the local key or an exported public key kept outside the vault (`--public-key`)
Stores an attestation as a shared store record on a switched machine, so every machine holding shared lists it
Lists attestations newest first and verifies the newest one, from the CLI or MCP (`brain_attestations`)
limits: Signing refuses on a switched machine whose legacy log tree is gone; brain store records are never attested
Verification only reports, repairs nothing, and checks rows from the attested head forward
A lost private key stops new signing; past attestations stay verifiable while the public key survives

features.name: Secret custody
features.summary: Credentials kept encrypted behind a capability gate and referenced as $secret:NAME in configuration.
capabilities: Keeps values AES-256-GCM encrypted in a 0600 `secrets.json` beside a 0600 keyfile, in vault or device state
Takes a value from stdin or `--from-env`, never from the command line
Injects a secret as its env var into a command its glob allowlist matches (`secret run`), redacting output
Wraps the keyfile under a scrypt passphrase on the first `unlock`; `unwrap` writes the raw key back
Exports every entry as one passphrase-encrypted bundle and restores it (`secret export`, `secret import`)
Resolves `$secret:NAME` config references from the store first, then the environment; a locked entry raises
Reports `$secret:` refs (`secrets list`) or a name (`secrets status`) undecrypted; env only unless `--vault`
Logs every custody operation as an audit record that holds no value
limits: Does not protect against root or same-user processes on the host; there is no daemon or hardware key
A lost passphrase or keyfile leaves stored values unreadable; there is no recovery
Keeping the state directory out of a file-sync folder is left to the operator; only git exclusion is written
The MCP tool can only list secrets and run allowlisted commands

features.name: Snapshots and rollback
features.summary: Recovery points before brain mutations, with diff and restore; on a store-switched machine rollback refuses.
capabilities: Archives `Brain/` (without `.snapshots`, `.artifacts`) as `.snapshots/<run_id>.tar.zst`, gzip without zstd
Takes a snapshot before every dream mutation and destructive write; a snapshot that fails aborts the operation
Keeps the newest `snapshots.retention_count` archives (default 10) and prunes the rest
Adds the search index only with `snapshots.include_derived_store` (off by default), within a size cap
Lists snapshots with reason, size, manifest and index coverage (`snapshot log`)
Diffs two snapshots, or one and live `Brain/`, per file; preferences and retired per field (`snapshot diff`)
Refuses `rollback` when the live tree drifted from the snapshot manifest unless `--force-rollback`; asks first
Archives the live tree as a recovery point before restoring, and never touches `.snapshots/` on restore
limits: On a machine switched to the store a snapshot holds only device-local state; rollback and live diff refuse
Covers the `Brain/` tree only, not other notes of the vault
Creating a snapshot needs a system `tar` except on Windows

features.name: Multi-agent provenance
features.summary: Shows which agent contributed which signals and notes, compares agents, and groups signals by source.
capabilities: Collects per-agent contributions of four kinds: signals, preferences, log events and note writes
Filters them by agents, topic, free text, kind and limit (default 50) and returns a per-agent roster
Compares agents in browse, search, diff or map mode, listing the topics they share and those unique to each
Groups signals by agent and source type with active, processed, archived and topic counts (`brain sources`)
Withholds contributions outside the caller's owner scope or reach before the roster is counted
limits: Read-only; it assigns and changes no attribution
Without a per-agent MCP token attribution is caller-asserted; note writes name the writer's configured agent

features.name: Answer quote check
features.summary: At the end of a turn, checks the agent's quoted spans against the notes the turn actually had.
capabilities: Finds quoted spans in the turn's last assistant messages at Stop and checks each against the turn's notes
Uses the note a span cites (wikilink or path), else the notes the injection ledger says entered this session
Gives each span one verdict: verified, not-in-note, source-truncated, note-unavailable or not-text
Runs per phase (recall, active, subagent) in `quote_check.<phase>` mode off, shadow (default) or enforce
Names the unverified spans to the model in one note
Appends one `reply_presence` record per checked turn: per injected note, verified, its worst miss or absent
Turns off entirely with `quote_check_enabled: false` in the machine config
limits: Never blocks or edits the answer; a verdict is reported, not enforced
Codex reads no Stop annotation, so only records and enforce events remain; Grok Build never runs the check
The recall phase runs only when `recall_inject_enabled` is on

features.name: Secret redaction and egress guard
features.summary: Masks secret-shaped values in what is written, logged or reported; every export path passes one egress guard.
capabilities: Masks values of secret-named keys (api_key, token, password, private_key, ...) as `***REDACTED***`
Finds them in env assignments, YAML and log lines, JSON entries and `Authorization: Bearer` headers
Strips `<private>...</private>` regions from signal fields first; an unclosed tag strips to the field's end
Marks text past its 1 MiB scan window as only partly scanned instead of passing the tail as clean
Passes every export verb through one egress guard: it redacts each string, refuses one it cannot scan whole
Declares every path sending vault bytes out in one registry; a census test fails on an undeclared one
Scrubs public IPs, URL credentials, host:port endpoints and internal host names from parked MCP results
Replaces the vault root in MCP error messages, and the home and temp roots too for a remote caller
limits: A signal's raw quote is kept only to 4096 characters, after `<private>` stripping and redaction
Five declared network paths send unscanned: two embedding providers, the reranker, Telegram, research
Redaction is pattern-based and narrow; output meant for other people still needs a look first

features.name: Safe file writes
features.summary: Keeps every write inside the vault and atomic, serializes writers with locks and refuses links planted in local state.
capabilities: Routes every vault write through one check that refuses `..`, an absolute path or a link out of the vault
Checks a path carried by a synced record before it names a file: it must stay relative and inside its folder
Writes a file as a sibling temp file, fsyncs it, renames it over the target and fsyncs the folder
Takes each lock as an exclusively created name and waits out a held one within that lock's budget
Records each store lock's holder (process, command, time) beside it and names it when a wait runs out
Retries the longest-waiting store writer soonest, and takes over a lock directory older than 60 s by age
Treats a name Windows still holds as delete pending as a held lock, not as an error
Refuses state in `.open-second-brain/` when a folder on the way is a symbolic link; never follows a leaf link
Stops the vault's writers on this machine while a brain store migration of that vault runs there
Reports a vault it cannot examine as one `vault_unreadable` error over MCP and one line with exit 1 on the CLI
limits: An atomic write covers one file; a write of several files is not rolled back across them
The migration gate is device-local and stops writers on the migrating machine only
A search on a legacy machine still records its activation files in `Brain/search/` during a migration

features.name: Agent identity
features.summary: Names the agent behind signals, evidence and log lines from an argument, a token or the config; stamps the process kind.
capabilities: Strips a leading `@` from a caller-named agent and drops generic guesses such as `assistant` or `model`
Attributes a token caller's signals, evidence, log lines, expirations and ingests to that token's agent
Judges a token caller's note writes as that token's agent in the permissions document and the owner gate
Otherwise takes a missing agent from the configured `agent_name`, as every note-write record always does
Refuses a named agent that differs from the one a per-agent token binds; the shared key may name any agent
Derives a host-qualified name per runtime from an operator name of the form `<vendor>-<host>-agent`
Names a dispatched subagent after its delegator plus the subagent id the host gives it
Reminds the agent of its name and fitting writer tool every turn through OpenClaw's and Hermes's prompt hooks
Gives the same reminder on Claude Code and Codex through their post-write hook
Stamps each record with its process kind (`origin_channel`: `mcp-tool`, `cli`, `import`), never an argument
limits: Without a per-agent token the agent name is what the caller asserted; it is not authenticated
Records written before the origin stamp carry none and are not backfilled

features.name: Remote read reservation
features.summary: Private pages and private-partition lane entries are withheld from remote callers; reach is a transport fact.
capabilities: Sets reach in the transport: stdio, the CLI and a loopback HTTP bind are local; other HTTP requests are remote
Withholds pages with the reserved `private` visibility token from remote search, page walks and path reads
Lets `--visibility` only narrow results; the reserved token outranks the other tokens on the same page
Refuses a reach argument in any spelling; `integrity.owner_scope_delivery: fail` refuses a foreign owner scope
Gives a remote caller vault-relative paths and named placeholders, never an absolute path of the host
Counts reserved pages and the note-returning surfaces that do not yet consult the field (`search check`)
Withholds lane entries of the private partition from remote lists, shows, counts and names
Refuses a remote create or overwrite that meets a private entry with one fixed answer naming nothing
A remote removal or move of a private entry finds it absent; a folder with a private member is refused whole
Keeps new receipts, log events and ledger rows that name a private lane entry in the private partition
limits: Local reach proves file-equivalent access or a request from this host, not the operator's intent
A vault that never writes the reserved token behaves as before
While the store cannot be read whole, a remote caller's lane reads answer as empty
Older records that named a private entry keep their shared copies on peers that already synced them
